# NYC Motor Vehicle Collisions — Crashes

Source: NYC Open Data, dataset `h9gi-nx95` ("Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes"), published by the NYPD. Snapshot downloaded 2026-10-03.

Official description (paraphrased): each row is one police-reported motor vehicle collision in New York City. A police report (MV-104AN) is required when someone is injured or killed, or when there is at least $1,000 of damage. The data is preliminary and subject to change.

File: `crashes.parquet` (one row per crash)

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| collision_id | BIGINT | Unique identifier of the crash |
| crash_date | DATE | Date of the crash |
| crash_time | TIME | Time of the crash |
| borough | VARCHAR | Borough where the crash occurred |
| zip_code | VARCHAR | Postal code of the crash location |
| latitude, longitude | DOUBLE | Coordinates of the crash location |
| location | VARCHAR | Latitude/longitude pair |
| on_street_name | VARCHAR | Street on which the crash occurred |
| cross_street_name | VARCHAR | Nearest cross street |
| off_street_name | VARCHAR | Street address if known |
| number_of_persons_injured / _killed | INTEGER | People injured / killed |
| number_of_pedestrians_injured / _killed | INTEGER | Pedestrians injured / killed |
| number_of_cyclist_injured / _killed | INTEGER | Cyclists injured / killed |
| number_of_motorist_injured / _killed | INTEGER | Vehicle occupants injured / killed |
| contributing_factor_vehicle_1 … _5 | VARCHAR | Factor contributing to the crash, for each vehicle involved |
| vehicle_type_code1 … 5 | VARCHAR | Type of each vehicle involved |

import duckdb
conn = duckdb.connect()
result = conn.execute("""
SELECT 
  min(crash_date) as min_date,
  max(crash_date) as max_date,
  count(*) as total_crashes,
  sum(number_of_cyclist_injured) as total_cyclist_injured,
  sum(number_of_cyclist_killed) as total_cyclist_killed,
  sum(case when number_of_cyclist_injured > 0 or number_of_cyclist_killed > 0 then 1 else 0 end) as cyclist_crashes,
  sum(number_of_cyclist_injured + number_of_cyclist_killed) as total_cyclist_casualties
FROM './data/crashes.parquet'
""").fetchall()
print(result)

python3 << 'PY'
import duckdb
import pandas as pd
import os
os.makedirs('./out', exist_ok=True)

conn = duckdb.connect()
df = conn.execute("""
SELECT 
  year(crash_date) as year,
  sum(number_of_cyclist_injured) as cyclist_injured,
  sum(number_of_cyclist_killed) as cyclist_killed,
  sum(case when number_of_cyclist_injured > 0 or number_of_cyclist_killed > 0 then 1 else 0 end) as cyclist_crashes,
  count(*) as total_crashes
FROM './data/crashes.parquet'
WHERE year(crash_date) >= 2012 AND year(crash_date) <= 2026
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year
""").df()

df['cyclist_casualties'] = df['cyclist_injured'] + df['cyclist_killed']
df['casualties_per_cyclist_crash'] = df['cyclist_casualties'] / df['cyclist_crashes'].replace(0,1)
df.to_csv('./out/cyclist_safety_by_year.csv', index=False)
print(df.to_string())

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import os

df = pd.read_csv('./out/cyclist_safety_by_year.csv')
# Focus on full years - exclude 2026 since it's partial
df_full = df[df['year'] < 2026].copy()

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 10))
fig.suptitle('Cyclist Safety in NYC Over Time (2012-2025)', fontsize=14)

# Cyclist crashes
axes[0,0].plot(df_full['year'], df_full['cyclist_crashes'], marker='o')
axes[0,0].set_title('Cyclist Crashes per Year')
axes[0,0].set_xlabel('Year')
axes[0,0].set_ylabel('Number of Crashes')

# Cyclist killed
axes[0,1].plot(df_full['year'], df_full['cyclist_killed'], marker='o', color='red')
axes[0,1].set_title('Cyclist Fatalities per Year')
axes[0,1].set_xlabel('Year')
axes[0,1].set_ylabel('Fatalities')

# Cyclist injuries
axes[1,0].plot(df_full['year'], df_full['cyclist_injured'], marker='o', color='orange')
axes[1,0].set_title('Cyclist Injuries per Year')
axes[1,0].set_xlabel('Year')
axes[1,0].set_ylabel('Injuries')

# Casualties per crash
axes[1,1].plot(df_full['year'], df_full['casualties_per_cyclist_crash'], marker='o', color='purple')
axes[1,1].set_title('Cyclist Casualties per Crash')
axes[1,1].set_xlabel('Year')
axes[1,1].set_ylabel('Casualties per Crash')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('./out/cyclist_safety_trends.png')
print('Saved ./out/cyclist_safety_trends.png')

part.text:
The data shows cyclist safety in NYC has a mixed trend from 2012-2025. Total cyclist crashes and injuries rose from 2012 (2202 crashes, 2210 injured) to peaks around 2019 (4964 crashes, 4986 injured), dropped during 2020, and have since remained elevated above early 2010s levels (5279 crashes, 5358 injured in 2025). Fatalities have been highly variable with spikes (31 in 2019, 31 in 2023) and remain concerning (23 in 2025). Injury/fatality rates per cyclist crash have increased slightly over time, suggesting crashes may be becoming more severe on average. Overall, by raw numbers cyclists are not clearly "safer" than they used to be compared to the early 2010s - crash and injury counts are much higher, while fatalities show no consistent downward trend.
